narratives.name: Team Topologies Team Design
narratives.description: Team Topologies context for Team alpha progression.

narrativeContexts.context: Team Topologies treats the team as the fundamental unit of delivery, not individuals, with team-first thinking applied to all design decisions including software boundaries and cognitive load limits.

Four team types provide simplified vocabulary: stream-aligned teams own value streams end-to-end, platform teams reduce cognitive load via self-service, enabling teams temporarily boost capabilities, complicated-subsystem teams handle specialist complexity. Teams interact through three explicit modes (Collaboration, X-as-a-Service, Facilitating) with Team APIs defining interfaces. Cognitive load management ensures teams sized and scoped within human bandwidth limits (5-9 people, maximum 1 complex or 2-3 simple domains). Teams function as organizational sensors with performance metrics signaling when topology evolution needed.

Effective teams require stability (weeks-to-months), clear ownership boundaries, explicit interaction modes, and continuous cognitive load optimization to deliver fast flow and serve as foundation for intentional architecture through Conway's Law.

narratives.name: Platform as Product with TVP
narratives.description: Team Topologies context for Platform alpha progression.

narrativeContexts.context: The primary benefit of a platform is reducing cognitive load on stream-aligned teams through self-service capabilities that abstract infrastructure complexity, as emphasized by Martin Fowler's insight on Team Topologies.

Thinnest Viable Platform (TVP) is the careful balance between keeping platform small and ensuring it accelerates delivery, starting as simple as a wiki page and evolving based on pull from stream teams. Platform as Product treats internal developers as customers requiring product management discipline (discovery + delivery), DevEx focus, adoption measurement, and ROI demonstration. Platform Manifesto principles guide: teams & interactions over tools & functionality, adoption & engagement over mandates & standards, rich customer experience over technical prowess, open to change and collaboration to discover needs, unblocking via self-service, aiming for superlinear impact with sublinear growth. At scale, platforms compose from team-of-teams including stream-aligned teams building features, enabling teams supporting adoption, and lower-level platform teams providing infrastructure foundation.

Successful platforms measurably reduce cognitive load (25%+ context switching reduction), improve productivity (20%+ gains), and demonstrate clear ROI, with enabling teams critical for adoption and platform team structure following Team Topologies patterns.

narratives.name: Managing Team Cognitive Capacity
narratives.description: Cognitive load management as team design constraint.

narrativeContexts.context: Teams have finite cognitive capacity that gets exhausted when responsibilities exceed working memory limits, with three types of load (intrinsic task complexity, extraneous environment overhead, germane productive learning) requiring active management.

Cognitive load management applies domain heuristics (maximum 1 complex or 2-3 simple domains per team), platform abstraction as primary reduction mechanism for extraneous load (infrastructure concerns), consistent UX across services to minimize learning overhead, and regular assessments asking: Do you feel effective and able to respond timely? Overloaded teams make poor decisions and move slowly despite competence, with symptoms including context switching, inability to maintain mastery, and ineffectiveness despite skill. Platform teams measure success primarily through cognitive load reduction on stream teams (target 25% context switching decrease, 20% productivity gains).

Sustained cognitive load optimization requires continuous monitoring, threshold-based triggers for team boundary adjustments, and platform evolution prioritized by load reduction impact, enabling teams to maintain mastery and effectiveness.

narratives.name: Three Interaction Modes Framework
narratives.description: Three explicit patterns for team relationships.

narrativeContexts.context: Only three ways teams should interact, eliminating ambiguous coordination mandates and providing clear vocabulary for team relationships with different cognitive load costs and suitable contexts.

Collaboration mode suits discovery of new things (APIs, practices, technologies) with working closely together for defined period, high bandwidth but high cost, time-bounded with clear goals, limited to one collaboration per team at a time, leading to blurred boundaries and blended software responsibilities through Conway's Law. X-as-a-Service mode enables consuming well-defined component with minimal interaction, clear ownership boundaries, predictable delivery, low cognitive load on consumer, requiring well-chosen service boundaries and excellent DevEx (usability, reliability, versioning, documentation). Facilitating mode involves one team helping another learn/adopt practices/overcome impediments, empowerment focus making teams self-sufficient, no direct system building by facilitator, typical for enabling teams assisting stream-aligned teams. Interaction modes evolve over time with discovery phases using collaboration for learning, establishment phases reducing collaboration, mature phases transitioning to XaaS as solutions stabilize. Research shows intermittent (not constant) collaboration improves collective problem-solving.

Explicit interaction modes with strategic evolution enable fast flow by minimizing wasteful coordination while preserving necessary collaboration, with modes serving as organizational sensors signaling topology adjustment needs.

narratives.name: Teams as Organizational Sensors
narratives.description: Continuous adaptation through feedback mechanisms.

narrativeContexts.context: Organizational design is never done but must evolve as business, technology, and people change, with small frequent adjustments preventing organizational debt accumulation requiring crisis reorganizations, enabled by teams functioning as sensors.

Teams become sensors through systematic collection of performance metrics (deployment frequency, lead time, MTTR, velocity, cycle time, WIP), cognitive load assessments, and interaction pattern monitoring. Evolution triggers signal when topology adjustments needed including software exceeding team capacity (organization size approaching Dunbar limits, single bottleneck team, internal specialization becoming constraint), delivery cadence degradation (longer cycles, decreased velocity, increased WIP, growing dependencies, technical debt), and complex service dependencies (numerous integrations, poor DevEx, inconsistent telemetry). The Three Ways of DevOps provide sensing infrastructure with flow from dev to ops (deployment metrics), feedback from ops to dev (MTTR, error rates inform priorities), and continuous experimentation (safe-to-fail learning). IT operations becomes rich source of high-fidelity organizational signals when properly integrated with continuity of care ensuring teams own full lifecycle. Small incremental changes occur monthly based on signals rather than massive annual reorganizations, with teams negotiating boundary adjustments based on local knowledge.

Mature organizations achieve cybernetic self-steering with predictable evolution responding to environmental signals, operational feedback systematically driving development priorities, and architecture-organization co-evolution as sustained competitive advantage.

narrativeContexts.context: Team Topologies provides simplified organizational vocabulary with four fundamental types (Stream-Aligned, Platform, Enabling, Complicated-Subsystem) as alternative to traditional hierarchies, designed to optimize value flow and software architecture through intentional communication structures.

Topology design applies fracture planes to define team boundaries with Domain-Driven Design bounded contexts as primary split, plus regulatory compliance, change cadence, team location, risk profile, performance isolation, technology (cautiously), and user personas as additional fracture planes. Reverse Conway Maneuver intentionally designs team intercommunication before software finalization to achieve target architecture with restricted communication between teams that should have loosely coupled components. Team boundaries must align with cognitive capacity using domain heuristics (maximum 1 complex or 2-3 simple domains per team), avoiding monolithic anti-patterns (application, database, model, thinking, workplace monoliths). Organizational sensing enables continuous evolution through small incremental adjustments monthly based on triggers (software exceeding capacity, delivery cadence degradation, complex service dependencies) rather than massive annual reorganizations. Context factors considered include technical/cultural maturity, organization size, software scale, and engineering discipline strength.

Mature topology design achieves predictable architectural outcomes through deliberate team structure, sustained fast flow with minimal dependencies, and self-steering adaptation to environment changes as competitive advantage.

activities.name: Design Team Topology
activities.description: Architect organizational team structure using four fundamental types and boundary principles.

narratives.name: Designing Team Topology Technique
narratives.description: How to design team structure using four fundamental types.

narrativeContexts.context: Design Team Topology
Organizations need to structure teams intentionally to optimize value flow and software architecture rather than relying on traditional hierarchical org charts.
Static team structures create bottlenecks, dependencies, and misalignment between communication patterns and desired system architecture.

Apply four fundamental team types (Stream-Aligned, Platform, Enabling, Complicated-Subsystem) with cognitive load limits, use fracture planes (Domain-Driven Design bounded contexts, regulatory compliance, change cadence, risk profile) to define boundaries, apply Reverse Conway Maneuver to design team intercommunication before software finalization, and ensure teams sized 5-9 people with maximum 1 complex or 2-3 simple domains.
Clear team ownership of system components, intentional architecture through team structure, manageable cognitive load enabling team effectiveness, and foundation for continuous topology evolution.

activities.name: Define Team Interaction Modes
activities.description: Explicitly specify how teams interdepend using Collaboration, X-as-a-Service, or Facilitating patterns.

narratives.name: Defining Interaction Modes Technique
narratives.description: How to specify team relationships using three explicit modes.

narrativeContexts.context: Define Team Interaction Modes
Teams need clear understanding of how they should work together to avoid ambiguous coordination mandates and wasted effort.
Unclear team relationships lead to coordination confusion, excessive meetings, dependency bottlenecks, and misaligned expectations.

For each inter-team relationship, select one of three modes: Collaboration (discovery of new things, time-bounded with clear goals), X-as-a-Service (provider-consumer with well-defined boundaries and DevEx focus), or Facilitating (helping and mentoring toward self-sufficiency). Document mode selection on topology diagrams, plan mode evolution as systems mature (Collaboration transitions to XaaS), and recognize Conway's Law effects of each mode on architecture.
Explicit expectations between teams, minimized coordination overhead, appropriate cognitive load for each interaction type, and strategic architecture shaping through interaction mode choices.

activities.name: Assess Cognitive Load
activities.description: Evaluate team mental bandwidth capacity and identify overload risks or reduction opportunities.

narratives.name: Assessing Cognitive Load Technique
narratives.description: How to evaluate and manage team mental bandwidth.

narrativeContexts.context: Assess Cognitive Load
Teams have finite cognitive capacity that gets exhausted when responsibilities exceed working memory limits, impacting effectiveness regardless of competence.
Overloaded teams make poor decisions, move slowly, experience burnout, and cannot maintain mastery in their domains despite being skilled.

Ask teams: Do you feel effective and able to respond timely? Catalog domains assigned to each team and rate complexity (maximum 1 complex or 2-3 simple domains). Measure context-switching frequency, tool variety, integration points. Classify load types (intrinsic task complexity, extraneous environment overhead, germane productive learning). Identify platform abstraction opportunities to reduce extraneous load. Define thresholds triggering team boundary adjustments.

Teams scoped within cognitive capacity maintain effectiveness, platform identifies high-impact reduction opportunities, and continuous monitoring enables proactive load management preventing team overwhelm.

activities.name: Implement Platform as Product
activities.description: Apply product management discipline to platform treating developers as customers with DevEx focus.

narratives.name: Platform as Product Technique
narratives.description: How to treat platform as product with customer focus.

narrativeContexts.context: Implement Platform as Product
Platforms exist to reduce cognitive load on stream-aligned teams through self-service capabilities, requiring product thinking not just technology delivery.
Technology-centric platforms built without user research lead to poor adoption, wasted investment, and build it and they won't come failures.

Ask: Should this platform exist? Identify stream-aligned teams as customers. Apply product discovery to understand developer jobs-to-be-done. Prioritize roadmap by cognitive load reduction and DevEx impact not technology features. Measure adoption, investigate non-adoption, track productivity improvements (20%+ target). Apply Thinnest Viable Platform principle: only what measurably accelerates delivery. Follow Platform Manifesto: teams & interactions over tools, adoption over mandates, customer experience over technical prowess.
Platform demonstrably reduces stream team cognitive load, measurable productivity gains justify investment, high voluntary adoption, and clear ROI for business stakeholders.

activities.name: Apply Reverse Conway Maneuver
activities.description: Intentionally design team intercommunications before software finalization to achieve target architecture.

narratives.name: Reverse Conway Maneuver Technique
narratives.description: How to shape architecture through team structure design.

narrativeContexts.context: Apply Reverse Conway Maneuver
Conway's Law states organizations design systems mirroring their communication structures, creating homomorphic force between teams and architecture.
Accidental architecture emerges from unplanned team communication patterns, often creating monoliths or distributed monoliths regardless of intended modularity.

Define target software architecture with explicit modularity goals (loose coupling, high cohesion, clear boundaries). Design team structure and communication patterns to achieve that architecture. Align team boundaries with desired service boundaries. Restrict communication between teams that should have loosely coupled components. Establish Team APIs defining exact interfaces. Implement organizational structure before major coding begins. Monitor whether emerging architecture matches design, adjust team interactions if unwanted coupling appears.

Software architecture emerges as designed rather than accidentally, modular loosely-coupled systems sustained over time, team autonomy enabled through clear boundaries, and architecture quality directly attributable to intentional team structure.

activities.name: Establish Organizational Sensing
activities.description: Create feedback mechanisms enabling continuous topology adaptation through team performance signals.

narratives.name: Organizational Sensing Technique
narratives.description: How to enable continuous topology evolution through feedback.

narrativeContexts.context: Establish Organizational Sensing
Organizational design is never done but must evolve as business, technology, and people change, requiring systematic feedback mechanisms.
Static team structures accumulate organizational debt leading to crisis reorganizations, with no systematic way to know when topology adjustments needed.

Implement The Three Ways of DevOps as sensing infrastructure: optimize flow (deployment metrics), create feedback from ops to dev (MTTR, error rates), enable experimentation. Establish teams as sensors collecting deployment frequency, velocity, cycle time, WIP, cognitive load assessments, dependency wait times. Define evolution triggers: software exceeding team capacity (Dunbar limits, bottlenecks), delivery cadence degradation (longer cycles, increased WIP), complex service dependencies (numerous integrations, poor DevEx). Make small monthly adjustments instead of massive annual reorganizations. Allow teams to negotiate boundary changes based on local knowledge.

Topology evolves predictably in response to environmental signals, small incremental changes prevent organizational debt, operational feedback drives development priorities, and organizational agility becomes sustained competitive advantage.

activities.name: Define Thinnest Viable Platform
activities.description: Scope platform capabilities to just enough to accelerate delivery without excessive complexity.

narratives.name: Thinnest Viable Platform Technique
narratives.description: How to scope platform to essential capabilities only.

narrativeContexts.context: Define Thinnest Viable Platform
Platform exists to reduce cognitive load on stream teams, requiring careful balance between keeping it small and ensuring it accelerates delivery.
Over-engineered platforms with excessive capabilities create their own complexity burden, while under-scoped platforms fail to unblock stream teams.

Start with simplest viable platform: possibly just wiki documenting cloud provider and service choices. Progress only when stream teams demonstrate need. Ask: Should this platform exist? Does this capability measurably accelerate delivery? Identify high-impact cognitive load reducers: abstract provisioning, monitoring, deployment, security from stream teams. Apply pull model: let demand drive evolution not feature push. Resist scope creep: each capability must pass acceleration and load reduction tests. Target superlinear impact with sublinear growth.

Platform remains minimal yet effective, stream teams measurably accelerated, cognitive load demonstrably reduced (25%+ context switching decrease), and platform justifies existence through clear value delivery.

activities.name: Evolve Team Boundaries
activities.description: Continuously adapt team structure based on organizational sensing signals and evolution triggers.

narratives.name: Evolving Team Boundaries Technique
narratives.description: How to adapt team structure continuously based on signals.

narrativeContexts.context: Evolve Team Boundaries
Team structures must evolve continuously as environment changes rather than remaining fixed until crisis forces painful reorganization.
Static team boundaries accumulate organizational debt, creating bottlenecks, misaligned responsibilities, and architectural coupling over time.

Monitor organizational sensing signals identifying when software exceeds team capacity, delivery cadence degrades, or service dependencies become complex. When triggers fire, make small incremental adjustments monthly: split overloaded teams, create platform abstractions, add enabling teams, adjust boundaries. Allow teams to negotiate changes based on local knowledge rather than imposing top-down decisions. Document evolution path showing snapshots over time with rationale for each change. Maintain team stability (weeks to months) between adjustments to preserve shared context.

Topology adapts predictably to environmental changes, organizational debt prevented through continuous small adjustments, team effectiveness sustained, and architecture co-evolves with organization structure.

activities.name: Identify Business Opportunities
activities.description: Recognize organizational flow constraints and architecture misalignment as transformation drivers.

narratives.name: Identifying Business Opportunities Technique
narratives.description: How to recognize topology transformation drivers.

narrativeContexts.context: Identify Business Opportunities
Organizational bottlenecks, cognitive load issues, and architecture-team misalignment signal transformation opportunities through Team Topologies framework.
Teams experiencing dependency wait times, overwhelm from excessive responsibilities, and software structures not matching desired modularity limit business agility and time-to-market.

Assess current topology against four fundamental team types revealing structural gaps. Baseline flow metrics including deployment frequency, lead time, and dependency wait times as quantification starting point. Quantify cognitive load through team bandwidth utilization and domain complexity documentation per team. Articulate value proposition with expected productivity gains (20%+ target) and deployment improvements (40%+ failure reduction). Recognize architecture-team misalignment where software structure diverges from intended modularity due to communication patterns.

Clear quantified business opportunity with baseline metrics, value proposition showing measurable ROI through productivity and deployment improvements, and recognized need for topology evolution versus one-time reorganization.

activities.name: Validate Topology Viability
activities.description: Confirm organizational change capacity and secure evolution budget for continuous adaptation.

narratives.name: Validating Topology Viability Technique
narratives.description: How to confirm transformation feasibility.

narrativeContexts.context: Validate Topology Viability
Topology evolution requires sustained organizational change capacity and budget commitment beyond one-time reorganization mindset.
Insufficient funding or lack of leadership commitment to continuous adaptation causes topology initiatives to fail or revert to static structures.

Secure topology evolution budget for team restructuring, enabling teams, and platform capabilities development. Confirm organizational change capacity with leadership commitment to continuous topology adaptation versus treating it as one-time project. Validate that fast flow improvements are measurable through deployment frequency increases and dependency wait time reductions. Demonstrate cognitive load reduction via team effectiveness surveys targeting 25%+ context switching decrease. Show architecture alignment improvement as Reverse Conway Maneuver takes effect with software modularity matching team boundaries.

Funded evolution initiative with organizational change capacity confirmed, measurable improvements in flow and cognitive load demonstrating viability, and architecture-team alignment evidencing transformation effectiveness.

activities.name: Measure Topology Benefits
activities.description: Track sustained productivity gains and organizational agility competitive advantage from topology evolution.

narratives.name: Measuring Topology Benefits Technique
narratives.description: How to demonstrate sustained transformation value.

narrativeContexts.context: Measure Topology Benefits
Long-term topology transformation value requires demonstrating sustained productivity gains, deployment excellence, and organizational agility as competitive advantage.
Without sustained measurement, topology benefits fade over time as organizational debt accumulates and initial improvements erode.

Track sustained productivity gains maintaining 20%+ improvements over multiple quarters, not just initial spike. Measure deployment excellence with 40% failure reduction and 35% MTTR decrease sustained as baseline performance. Monitor organizational agility capability with topology evolution frequency, time from trigger to adjustment, and market responsiveness as strategic differentiator. Review quarterly trends to detect erosion early before crisis develops. Communicate business value to leadership demonstrating ROI continuation beyond initial transformation phase.
Proven long-term value sustaining investment, organizational agility recognized as competitive advantage, and continuous improvement culture preventing topology stagnation.

activities.name: Establish Team Collaboration Practices
activities.description: Define explicit collaboration patterns with clear goals and durations for team effectiveness.

narratives.name: Establishing Team Collaboration Technique
narratives.description: How to enable effective team collaboration.

narrativeContexts.context: Establish Team Collaboration Practices
Teams need explicit collaboration patterns defining interaction modes, value stream alignment, platform capabilities, and Team APIs for effective collaboration.
Unclear collaboration expectations lead to ambiguous coordination, missed hand-offs, duplicated work, and ineffective team interactions wasting cognitive capacity.

Define interaction modes explicitly as Collaboration, X-as-a-Service, or Facilitating for every relationship. For stream-aligned teams, establish end-to-end business domain ownership without hand-offs. For platform teams, scope self-service offerings based on stream team cognitive load reduction needs. Document Team APIs specifying code interfaces, versioning, practices, communication norms, and work visibility. Time-bound collaboration modes with clear discovery goals and durations to prevent permanent high-cost interactions.

Clear team collaboration patterns with explicit interaction modes, value stream alignment enabling autonomy, platform capabilities targeting load reduction, and documented Team APIs formalizing interfaces.

activities.name: Transition Team Ownership
activities.description: Manage enabling team mission completion and topology evolution through boundary changes.

narratives.name: Transitioning Team Ownership Technique
narratives.description: How to manage team dissolution and transitions.

narrativeContexts.context: Transition Team Ownership
Enabling teams complete missions and rotate to new challenges, while topology evolution requires team restructuring and boundary changes based on organizational sensing.
Unplanned team dissolution disrupts organizational memory and capability, while delayed transitions prevent topology evolution needed for sustained effectiveness.

For enabling teams, confirm capability adoption achieved with consumer teams demonstrating self-sufficiency before rotating to new challenges. Document lessons learned and knowledge transfer before team moves on. For topology evolution, validate that organizational sensing signals justify team restructuring or boundary changes. Plan transitions with continuity ensuring no ownership gaps or duplicated responsibilities. Communicate changes transparently with clear rationale tied to performance metrics. Maintain team stability (weeks-to-months) between changes to preserve shared context and effectiveness.

Successful enabling team missions with capability adoption sustained, planned topology evolution maintaining organizational effectiveness, and smooth transitions preserving institutional knowledge while enabling necessary change.

activities.name: Adopt Team Working Agreements
activities.description: Implement collaboration and X-as-a-Service practices with facilitating relationships.

narratives.name: Adopting Team Working Agreements Technique
narratives.description: How to implement team interaction practices.

narrativeContexts.context: Adopt Team Working Agreements
Interaction mode practices must transition from theory to daily application with time-bounded collaboration, excellent X-as-a-Service DevEx, and autonomy-building facilitation.
Defined interaction modes fail to deliver value without practical adoption, leading to collaboration drift, poor service experience, and dependent relationships instead of empowerment.

Time-bound collaboration with clear discovery goals and duration limits, restricting each team to maximum one collaboration at a time to manage cognitive load. Ensure X-as-a-Service provides excellent DevEx through clear APIs, self-service capabilities, and predictable delivery. Structure facilitating to build consumer autonomy not permanent dependency, with enabling teams working toward self-sufficiency. Document working agreements specifying interaction expectations, communication patterns, and success criteria. Review effectiveness regularly adjusting practices based on team feedback and performance metrics.

Interaction modes delivering intended value with collaboration focused and time-limited, X-as-a-Service providing outstanding developer experience, and facilitating successfully building team autonomy.

activities.name: Embed Team Practices
activities.description: Establish strategic interaction mode evolution with You Built It You Run It continuity.

narratives.name: Embedding Team Practices Technique
narratives.description: How to mature interaction mode practices.

narrativeContexts.context: Embed Team Practices
Mature practices require strategic interaction mode evolution as systems stabilize, with continuity of care ensuring teams own full lifecycles.
Static interaction modes prevent optimization as contexts change, while build-versus-run separation causes repeated mistakes from lost operational learning.

Evolve interaction modes strategically with collaboration transitioning to X-as-a-Service as systems stabilize and boundaries clarify. Enable teams facilitate then disengage as consumer autonomy achieved. Implement You Built It You Run It continuity with teams owning full lifecycle preventing handoff-induced knowledge loss. Apply intermittent collaboration pattern based on research showing intermittent (not constant) collaboration improves innovation. Minimize wasteful coordination through optimized interaction patterns while preserving essential collaboration. Use organizational sensing to drive way of working adjustments based on cognitive load data and performance signals.

Strategic mode evolution mastered with automatic adjustments, DevEx metrics excellence from platform services, organizational sensing feedback driving improvements, and minimal wasteful coordination sustaining effectiveness.

activities.name: Retire Outdated Practices
activities.description: Sunset interaction practices as topology evolves beyond pattern relevance.

narratives.name: Retiring Outdated Practices Technique
narratives.description: How to sunset obsolete practices gracefully.

narrativeContexts.context: Retire Outdated Practices
Topology evolution makes specific interaction practices obsolete as organizational structure changes, requiring graceful practice retirement.
Continuing obsolete practices wastes effort on irrelevant coordination while preventing teams from adopting practices suited to new topology.

Recognize when topology evolved past specific practice pattern with organizational structure changes making interaction practices obsolete. Capture lessons learned from retiring practice documenting what worked, what didn't, and key insights for future topology decisions. Complete team transitions to new interaction modes and working arrangements ensuring everyone understands replacements. Document evolution in playbook showing pattern lifecycle and triggers prompting retirement. Communicate changes clearly explaining why obsolete and what replaces it. Archive practice documentation for organizational memory without imposing continued use.
Clean practice retirement with lessons captured for future use, teams successfully transitioned to new arrangements, and organizational memory preserved while enabling topology evolution.

activities.name: Evolve Platform Capabilities
activities.description: Continuously improve platform through product discovery and pull-based evolution.

narratives.name: Evolving Platform Capabilities Technique
narratives.description: How to continuously improve platform as product.

narrativeContexts.context: Evolve Platform Capabilities
Platforms must evolve continuously through product discovery with stream teams, expanding TVP via pull signals rather than feature push.
Stagnant platforms fail to address emerging stream team needs, while feature-push expansion creates capabilities nobody wants or uses.

Conduct ongoing product discovery through regular user research with stream teams identifying jobs-to-be-done and pain points. Expand TVP via pull signals with capabilities added based on stream team demand not platform team feature push. Rotate enabling teams through adoption challenges as platform matures, supporting capability uptake and identifying friction. Scale platform composition with team-of-teams structure including stream-aligned teams building platform features, enabling teams supporting adoption, and sub-platform teams providing infrastructure foundation. Prioritize roadmap by cognitive load reduction impact not technical sophistication. Measure evolution success through adoption rates, DevEx metrics, and productivity improvements sustained.

Platform continuously improving based on actual user needs, TVP expanding through validated demand, enabling teams facilitating adoption, and platform composition scaling sustainably as team-of-teams.

activities.name: Retire Platform Services
activities.description: Decommission platform with migration path and consumer transition support.

narratives.name: Retiring Platform Services Technique
narratives.description: How to decommission platform gracefully.

narrativeContexts.context: Retire Platform Services
Platforms require eventual retirement when replaced by successors or when organizational needs evolve beyond their design.
Unplanned platform decommissioning disrupts consuming stream teams, while delayed retirement wastes resources maintaining obsolete capabilities.

Identify migration path to successor platform or alternative approach with clear technical transition strategy. Plan stream team consumer transitions with adequate migration timeline and enabling team support. Provide replacement capabilities before decommissioning to prevent forcing teams into unsupported workarounds. Clarify platform team reassignment with members transitioning to new opportunities as platform winds down. Communicate timeline and support resources transparently to all consumers. Archive lessons learned documenting what worked, what didn't, and insights for future platform design. Measure transition success through complete consumer migration without productivity degradation.
Smooth platform retirement with consumers successfully migrated to successors, platform team members reassigned to valuable work, and organizational learning preserved for future platforms.

activities.name: Develop Organizational Change Strategy
activities.description: Design target topology with transition sequence and Conway's Law application plan.

narratives.name: Developing Organizational Change Strategy Technique
narratives.description: How to plan topology evolution comprehensively.

narrativeContexts.context: Develop Organizational Change Strategy
Topology evolution requires comprehensive strategy with target state, incremental transition path, Conway's Law application, and enabling team support.
Ad hoc topology changes without strategy create chaos, while massive reorganizations disrupt productivity and lose institutional knowledge.

Design target topology with future team structure using four team types and explicit interaction modes mapped against desired architecture. Map transition sequence with small incremental changes scheduled over time avoiding massive disruptive reorganization. Plan Conway's Law intentional application through team communication design shaping desired software architecture. Identify enabling teams needed to facilitate capability building during transition phases. Define evolution triggers and thresholds signaling when adjustments needed based on organizational sensing. Allocate evolution budget for continuous topology adaptation not just one-time change project. Communicate vision and sequence transparently with rationale tied to business outcomes and flow improvements.

Comprehensive evolution strategy with clear target state, incremental transition path, Conway's Law leverage planned, enabling resources allocated, and organizational alignment on transformation journey.

activities.name: Optimize Team Cognitive Load
activities.description: Continuously monitor and adjust cognitive load maintaining optimal team effectiveness.

narratives.name: Optimizing Team Cognitive Load Technique
narratives.description: How to maintain optimal cognitive load continuously.

narrativeContexts.context: Optimize Team Cognitive Load
Sustained team effectiveness requires ongoing cognitive load monitoring and adjustment preventing capacity exceedance through proactive management.
Cognitive load degrades over time as responsibilities accumulate, technology changes, and team capabilities evolve, eventually overwhelming teams despite initial proper scoping.

Conduct regular cognitive load assessments tracking team health through periodic evaluations asking: Do you feel effective and able to respond timely? Define thresholds triggering team boundary adjustments when load exceeds limits based on domain heuristics and effectiveness metrics. Prioritize platform capabilities by cognitive load reduction impact with highest-impact abstractions developed first. Maintain domain mastery by ensuring teams sustain expertise in assigned areas without dilution from excessive scope. Measure and sustain productivity improvements at 20%+ effectiveness gains maintained over time as validation of optimization success. Use organizational sensing data to drive proactive adjustments before teams report overwhelm.

Sustained optimal cognitive load with teams maintaining effectiveness, threshold-based triggers preventing overwhelm, platform prioritized by reduction impact, domain mastery preserved, and productivity sustained long-term.

activities.name: Introduce Interaction Mode Concepts
activities.description: Educate organization on three interaction mode vocabulary and relationship labeling.

narratives.name: Introducing Interaction Mode Concepts Technique
narratives.description: How to introduce interaction mode vocabulary.

narrativeContexts.context: Introduce Interaction Mode Concepts
Organizations need clear vocabulary for team relationships eliminating ambiguous coordination mandates through three explicit interaction modes.
Vague mandates like collaborate effectively without specifics lead to coordination confusion, excessive meetings, and unclear expectations between teams.

Define three modes explicitly: Collaboration for discovery of new things with high bandwidth but high cost, X-as-a-Service for consuming well-defined components with minimal interaction, Facilitating for helping teams learn and overcome impediments toward self-sufficiency. Distinguish discovery versus consumption with Collaboration suited to learning while XaaS suited to predictable delivery. Recognize Facilitating as empowerment making teams self-sufficient not execution by facilitator. Begin labeling team relationships using mode vocabulary in topology diagrams and documentation. Educate leadership and teams on mode characteristics, suitable contexts, and cognitive load implications of each pattern.

Shared vocabulary for team interactions with three modes defined, relationships beginning to be labeled with mode names, and understanding of discovery-consumption distinction and facilitating empowerment purpose.

activities.name: Optimize Interaction Patterns
activities.description: Master interaction mode selection and evolution for flow with minimized dependency wait times.

narratives.name: Optimizing Interaction Patterns Technique
narratives.description: How to master interaction mode optimization.

narrativeContexts.context: Optimize Interaction Patterns
Mature organizations master interaction mode selection and evolution for maximum flow with minimized coordination waste and dependency bottlenecks.
Suboptimal interaction patterns create dependency wait times, excessive coordination overhead, and wasted cognitive capacity preventing flow despite proper team topology.

Apply intermittent collaboration pattern based on research showing intermittent (not constant) collaboration improves collective problem-solving and innovation. Achieve platform DevEx excellence with X-as-a-Service providing outstanding developer experience minimizing interaction cost through exceptional usability. Demonstrate measurable autonomy improvements from facilitating with consumer team self-sufficiency quantified through reduced support requests and independent capability growth. Eliminate dependency wait times through appropriate mode selection removing team-blocking bottlenecks. Use interaction patterns as organizational sensors with pattern changes signaling topology evolution needs. Monitor interaction effectiveness continuously adjusting modes based on performance data.

Mastered interaction optimization with intermittent collaboration driving innovation, platform DevEx excellence, measurable autonomy from facilitating, eliminated dependency bottlenecks, and interaction serving as evolution sensors.

activities.name: Begin Ad Hoc Sensing
activities.description: Initiate reactive topology adjustments recognizing structure impact on effectiveness.

narratives.name: Beginning Ad Hoc Sensing Technique
narratives.description: How to initiate reactive topology adjustment.

narrativeContexts.context: Begin Ad Hoc Sensing
Organizations transitioning from static structures begin recognizing that team design affects effectiveness, enabling reactive adjustments when problems severe.
Reactive adjustments only when severe create large disruptive changes and organizational churn, while lack of systematic monitoring delays recognition until crisis.

Recognize that organizational structure impacts team effectiveness with awareness that design matters not just execution. Make reactive changes when problems become severe enough to demand attention such as persistent bottlenecks or architectural failures. Document adjustments informally noting what prompted changes even without systematic data collection. Begin questioning whether structure or execution caused effectiveness issues. Acknowledge that large disruptive changes are painful but sometimes necessary before establishing continuous monitoring. Start informal observation of team dependencies, bottlenecks, and complaints as early warning signals even without metrics infrastructure yet.
Initial recognition that topology affects outcomes, reactive adjustments made when problems severe, and awareness building toward need for systematic sensing before establishing formal mechanisms.

activities.name: Adopt DevOps Practices
activities.description: Establish cross-functional teams and Conway's Law awareness as transitional bridge.

narratives.name: Adopting DevOps Practices Technique
narratives.description: How to establish DevOps as topology transition.

narrativeContexts.context: Adopt DevOps Practices
Organizations transitioning from functional silos use DevOps teams as bridge structure while developing Conway's Law awareness and cross-functional thinking.
Traditional Dev-QA-Ops silos create hand-off delays and knowledge barriers, while jumping directly to mature Team Topologies without transition overwhelms organizations.

Establish dedicated DevOps team as transitional bridge structure helping separate Development and Operations teams collaborate and learn cross-functional practices. Develop emerging Conway's Law awareness with beginning recognition that communication structure and architecture link together. Form some initial cross-functional product teams combining development and operations as experiments in end-to-end ownership. Focus on flow with value stream thinking beginning even if not yet systematic across organization. Accept that dependencies still block flow initially while working toward reduced wait times. Inventory teams and attempt fundamental type classification as preparation for mature topology. Recognize DevOps team as temporary scaffolding not permanent state moving toward stream-aligned and platform team clarity.

DevOps bridge team established enabling collaboration learning, Conway's Law awareness emerging, initial cross-functional teams formed, flow focus beginning, and foundation for mature Team Topologies adoption prepared.

Team Topology Map at Evolution Timeline level, Organizational Sensing Dashboard at Cybernetic Feedback System level, Team Interaction Contract at Living Agreement level.

patternViews.name: Fly - Cybernetic Self-Steering
patternViews.description: Mature organization with predictable evolution and architecture-organization co-evolution mastery.

narrativeContexts.context: Operational feedback systematically drives development priorities, continuity of care maintained with teams owning full lifecycle. Reverse Conway Maneuver consistently applied for architecture design, high autonomy with strategic alignment guardrails. Organization predictably adapts to market changes, technical architecture and team structure evolve together continuously. Team Topology Map at Dynamic Sensing Dashboard level, Organizational Sensing Dashboard at Predictive Organizational Intelligence level, Cognitive Load Assessment at Automated Optimization level. Organizational agility sustained as competitive advantage.

patterns.name: Conway's Law Strategic Application
patterns.description: Progressive application of Conway's Law from accidental to intentional architecture shaping.

patternViews.name: Prerequisites - Accidental Architecture
patternViews.description: Architecture emerges from unplanned team communication patterns.

narrativeContexts.context: Architecture emerges accidentally from team communication patterns without intentional design. Team structure follows traditional org chart patterns, architecture not aligned with desired modularity goals, monolithic systems result from everyone communicates with everyone pattern.

patternViews.name: Plan - Reverse Conway Maneuver Design
patternViews.description: Target architecture defined and team structure designed to achieve it.

narrativeContexts.context: Target software architecture defined with explicit modularity goals (loose coupling, high cohesion, clear service boundaries). Team boundaries aligned to desired system boundaries, team ownership maps to architectural components. Team intercommunication designed before coding, restricted communication enforces architectural boundaries. Team APIs define exact interfaces for components.

patternViews.name: Do - Implementation with Monitoring
patternViews.description: Teams structured and communicating as designed, with architecture emerging.

narrativeContexts.context: Team structure implemented with designed communication patterns. Team APIs established, interaction modes assigned (Collaboration for discovery, X-as-a-Service for established capabilities). Development proceeds with architectural boundaries matching team boundaries. Team Interaction Contract at Detailed Contract level ensures communication as designed.

patternViews.name: Check - Alignment Assessment
patternViews.description: Regular validation that architecture aligns with design and team structure supports it.

narrativeContexts.context: Architecture assessed to verify alignment with team structure. Service boundaries validated against team boundaries, architectural coupling problems traced to team communication, distributed monolith risks identified. Organizational sensing mechanisms monitor architecture-team alignment, technology choices evaluated for team autonomy impact.

patternViews.name: Act - Co-Evolution Refinement
patternViews.description: Adjust team structure and architecture together based on assessment findings.

narrativeContexts.context: Team boundaries and architecture adjusted together based on alignment assessment. Architectural changes prompt topology reviews, team changes planned considering architectural impact. Small incremental adjustments maintain alignment over time. Architecture and organization co-evolve continuously with predictable outcomes from deliberate team design. Modularity sustained through team structure, independent deployability enabled by team boundaries.

patterns.name: Platform as Product Maturity
patterns.description: Evolution from technology-centric platforms to value-driven products with demonstrated business impact.

patternViews.name: Prerequisites - No Platform Abstraction
patternViews.description: Stream teams manage all infrastructure directly with duplicated effort.

narrativeContexts.context: Every stream team provisions own infrastructure, no shared services or standardized capabilities, duplicated effort across teams for common needs. High cognitive load on stream teams for infrastructure concerns, no platform abstraction exists.

patternViews.name: Build - Platform Capability Creation
patternViews.description: Platform team builds initial self-service capabilities with product thinking.

narrativeContexts.context: Platform team established providing self-service capabilities. Stream-aligned teams identified as platform customers, basic purpose to support developers stated. Platform Capability Roadmap at Themed Capability Plan level, Platform as Product Charter at Customer Recognition level, Team API Documentation at Interface Catalog level. Platform capabilities grouped by theme with basic prioritization.

patternViews.name: Measure - Adoption and DevEx Tracking
patternViews.description: Platform measures adoption, DevEx, and cognitive load impact.

narrativeContexts.context: Platform tracking which teams using which capabilities, investigating non-adoption scenarios. Product discovery active with regular user research identifying jobs-to-be-done. DevEx measured through surveys and usability testing. 25% context switching reduction demonstrated as measurable cognitive load relief. Platform Capability Roadmap at Value-Driven Roadmap level, Platform as Product Charter at Product Discipline Charter level, Team API Documentation at Developer Experience Optimized level.

patternViews.name: Learn - Value Optimization
patternViews.description: Platform evolves based on measurable productivity and business impact.

narrativeContexts.context: Platform changes driven by productivity impact metrics, ROI for platform investment clearly demonstrated. 20%+ overall productivity improvements realized, enabling teams facilitate consistent platform adoption. Platform Capability Roadmap at Product Discovery Integration level, Platform as Product Charter at Value-Driven Product level. Non-adoption investigated and addressed, enabling teams critical for adoption.

patternViews.name: Scale - Strategic Business Platform
patternViews.description: Platform recognized as competitive advantage with superlinear impact.

narrativeContexts.context: Platform Manifesto principles fully adopted: teams & interactions over tools, adoption over mandates, customer experience over technical prowess. Superlinear impact with sublinear growth achieved, platform enables disproportionate value compared to team size. Business value relationship explicit in metrics, platform evolution aligned with business outcomes. Platform composition at scale with team-of-teams structure, golden path to production established. Platform-as-product recognized as competitive advantage. Platform Capability Roadmap at Adaptive Value Optimization level, Platform as Product Charter at Strategic Business Platform level.

patterns.name: Cognitive Load Optimization Path
patterns.description: Systematic reduction of team mental bandwidth taxation through platform abstraction and boundary design.

patternViews.name: Prerequisites - Overloaded Teams
patternViews.description: Teams spread thin across excessive responsibilities without load awareness.

narrativeContexts.context: Teams continually assigned new responsibilities without removals, no assessment of team capacity or domain complexity. Performance issues attributed to skill gaps not overload, frequent context switching across multiple domains. Teams report feeling overwhelmed but no action taken. Recognition of effectiveness problems as starting point.

patternViews.name: Introduction - Load Awareness
patternViews.description: Organization recognizes cognitive load as design constraint.

narrativeContexts.context: Leadership asks teams: Do you feel effective and able to respond timely? Cognitive load concepts introduced to team design conversations, distinction made between intrinsic, extraneous, germane load. Overload symptoms (slow decisions, errors) identified as capacity issues not skill problems. Cognitive Load Assessment at Qualitative Survey level.

patternViews.name: Body - Domain Boundaries and Platform Abstraction
patternViews.description: Team scopes limited and platform created to abstract infrastructure complexity.

narrativeContexts.context: Teams assigned maximum 1 complex domain or 2-3 simple domains, domain complexity assessed before assignment. Team boundaries align with cognitive capacity, responsibilities removed when new ones added. Platform abstractions identified for extraneous load reduction. Platform teams abstract infrastructure complexity (provisioning, monitoring, deployment), consistent UX across platform services reduces learning load, tooling rationalized to reduce variety overhead. Team APIs reduce integration cognitive cost. Cognitive Load Assessment at Quantified Load Analysis level, Team Topology Map showing platform teams, Platform Capability Roadmap at Value-Driven Roadmap level.

patternViews.name: Conclusion - Continuous Optimization
patternViews.description: Sustained cognitive load optimization with ongoing monitoring and platform evolution.

narrativeContexts.context: Regular cognitive load assessments conducted, thresholds trigger team boundary adjustments when load exceeds limits. Platform evolution prioritized by cognitive load reduction impact, teams maintain mastery in assigned domains. 20%+ productivity improvements sustained over time. Cognitive Load Assessment at Continuous Monitoring level, Platform Capability Roadmap at Adaptive Value Optimization level, Team API Documentation at Living Product Documentation level. Continuous optimization enables teams to maintain effectiveness.

patterns.name: Organizational Sensing and Adaptation
patterns.description: Building cybernetic feedback systems enabling continuous topology evolution.

patternViews.name: Situation - Static Organization
patternViews.description: Team structure fixed with no feedback mechanisms for adjustment.

narrativeContexts.context: Team boundaries permanent regardless of changing needs, no systematic gathering of team effectiveness signals. Reorganizations only happen during crisis or leadership change, performance degradation attributed to execution not structure. Organization recognizes need for continuous evolution capability.

patternViews.name: Task - Establish Sensing Mechanisms
patternViews.description: Create systems to capture team performance signals and identify evolution triggers.

narrativeContexts.context: Implement The Three Ways of DevOps as sensing infrastructure: optimize flow from development to operations, create feedback loops from operations to development, enable continuous experimentation. Establish teams as sensors collecting deployment frequency, velocity, cycle time, WIP, lead time, MTTR, change failure rate. Conduct regular cognitive load assessments, monitor inter-team interaction patterns and dependency wait times. IT operations recognized as rich source of high-fidelity organizational signals. Organizational Sensing Dashboard at Periodic Metrics Review level.

patternViews.name: Action - Trigger-Based Evolution
patternViews.description: Define triggers and make topology adjustments when signals indicate need.

narrativeContexts.context: Define evolution triggers: software exceeding team capacity (organization size approaching Dunbar limits, single bottleneck team, internal specialization constraint), delivery cadence degradation (longer cycles, decreased velocity, increased WIP, dependencies, technical debt), complex service dependencies (numerous integrations, poor DevEx, inconsistent telemetry). When triggers fire, conduct topology review: adjust team boundaries, create platform abstractions, form enabling teams. Make small incremental changes monthly rather than massive annual reorganizations. Teams negotiate boundary changes based on local knowledge. Organizational Sensing Dashboard at Trigger-Based Assessment level, Team Topology Map at Evolution Timeline level, Topology Evolution Playbook at Playbook with Scenarios level.

patternViews.name: Result - Cybernetic Self-Steering
patternViews.description: Organization predictably adapts with architecture-organization co-evolution.

narrativeContexts.context: Operational feedback systematically drives development priorities, continuity of care maintained with teams owning full lifecycle. Direct boundary negotiation by teams based on local knowledge, monthly evolution cadence as normal practice. Organizational agility sustained as competitive differentiator, architecture and organization structures evolve together continuously. Predictable evolution in response to environmental signals, sustained fast flow with high deployment frequency and low failure rates. Organizational Sensing Dashboard at Predictive Organizational Intelligence level, Team Topology Map at Dynamic Sensing Dashboard level, Topology Evolution Playbook at Self-Evolving System level.
